sections.title: Scalar--Mean Rigidity for Hyperbolic Balls in Dimensions 2≤n≤5
sections.abstract: The paper proves a non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions 2 through 5, adds a weighted Euclidean ball--torus rigidity result through total dimension 7, and gives a counterexample to the analogous hyperbolic product statement.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that, for the stated scalar-curvature and boundary-mean-curvature bounds, a nonzero-degree 1-Lipschitz boundary map to the corresponding hyperbolic sphere extends to an isometry with the hyperbolic ball (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact, connected, oriented smooth Riemannian manifold with connected nonempty boundary; dimension 2≤n≤5; scalar curvature at least −n(n−1); boundary mean curvature at least (n−1)coth ρ; boundary map targets the sphere of radius sinh ρ.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem stops at dimension 5; the paper also shows that a direct hyperbolic ball--torus analogue fails.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract identifies a low-dimensional case of a problem posed by Gromov and pairs it with a second rigidity theorem and a counterexample; the main theorem has a clearly checkable geometric scope.

sections.title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
sections.abstract: For a Griesmer code over a field of size q=p^f, the authors prove Ward's conjectured lower bound on the p-divisibility of all codeword weights in terms of the p-adic valuation of the minimum distance.
sections.claimed_result: If C is an [n,k,d]_q Griesmer code, q=p^f, and e=ν_p(d), then the authors prove ν_p(C)≥max{0,e−f+1} (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Linear q-ary code attaining the Griesmer bound; p is prime, q=p^f, and ν_p(C) is the minimum p-adic valuation of the nonzero codeword weights.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion is specific to Griesmer codes and does not classify divisibility for arbitrary linear codes.
sections.ranking_evidence: This is a stated proof of a named conjecture, and its cross-listing links a concrete coding-theory result to information theory.

sections.title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
sections.abstract: The authors derive regularity-dependent stability times for small Hamiltonian PDE solutions on the circle and construct examples with matching norm-amplification times, establishing sharpness under their analytic and arithmetic hypotheses.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove Gevrey and logarithmic ultra-differentiable stability scales, verify them for convolution NLS, fractional NLS with fixed noninteger exponent η>1/2, and a beam equation, and construct two fixed analytic nonlocal PDEs whose first prescribed norm amplification occurs on matching scales (arXiv abstract and Theorem 1.1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Small solutions on the one-dimensional torus; an analytic coefficient-majorant condition and a frequency/small-divisor hypothesis are required. The matching escape-time examples are for two specific analytic nonlocal Hamiltonian equations.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp upper-time examples are not established for every Hamiltonian PDE satisfying the stability hypotheses; the conclusions depend on the paper's arithmetic and regularity assumptions.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper combines lower stability bounds with matching upper-time examples, verifies hypotheses for several PDE families, and bridges analysis with dynamical systems.

sections.title: A well-posedness theory for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations and a class of global-in-time solutions
sections.abstract: The author proves critical-regularity local well-posedness for a symmetric class of 2D inhomogeneous Euler data, then obtains global solutions for a related one-dimensional reduction and a long-time density/relaxation dichotomy.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes local well-posedness for m-fold symmetric functions at critical regularity, and global well-posedness for a class of initial data in the reduced system with 0-homogeneous vorticity and density (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible Euler Cauchy problem; the local theorem assumes m-fold symmetry and permits velocity growth linear in space. The global theorem concerns the associated one-dimensional system and data away from equilibrium.
sections.unique_caveat: The global result is for a special reduced class, not general global well-posedness of the full 2D inhomogeneous Euler equations.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper connects a critical local theory to a nonperturbative global solution class and explicitly relates the local result to a problem posed by P. L. Lions.

sections.title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for L^p-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on R^2
sections.abstract: The authors settle endpoint attainment cases for a critical planar Moser--Trudinger variational problem and derive asymptotic expansions and profile limits for its extremals in several penalty regimes.
sections.claimed_result: Under the unit H^1(R^2) constraint, the authors prove attainment at the specified thresholds, a two-term expansion for p>4 as λ→∞, and strong subsequential convergence of rescaled centered radial extremals (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The functional has critical exponential e^{4πu²}, penalty λ|u|^p, and p≥2; asymptotic statements distinguish p>4 from the endpoint regimes and use centered radial extremals.
sections.unique_caveat: Several profile conclusions are subsequential and radial; the abstract does not assert uniqueness of extremizers.
sections.ranking_evidence: The abstract reports both endpoint existence and quantitative two-term asymptotics, with an exact transfer identity extending the conclusions to every constant planar norm.

sections.title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers within the set of squares
sections.abstract: The authors bound the number of integers n=2m²<X that fail to be a sum of two primes by X^{19/24+o(1)}.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the count of non-Goldbach numbers of the form 2m² below X is at most X^{19/24+o(1)} (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Integers of the special form n=2m² with n<X; the assertion is an upper bound on the exceptional set, not a statement that every such number is Goldbach.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimate leaves room for an infinite exceptional set and does not settle the Goldbach representation for each square-doubled integer.
sections.ranking_evidence: It gives a precise exceptional-set exponent for an additive-prime problem on a sparse structured sequence, a clean number-theoretic result with a readily testable quantitative statement.

sections.title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
sections.abstract: The authors prove empirical self-normalized concentration bounds for bounded observables of regenerative data and apply them to dependent-data classification and Gaussian approximation.
sections.claimed_result: For bounded functions of regenerative processes with i.i.d. marked cycles of finite mean length, the authors derive a self-normalized Bernstein inequality, classification generalization bounds, a minimax-optimal average-deviation bound in sample size and expected cycle length, and a Gaussian approximation with an observable block-variance estimator (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Regenerative process with independent identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length; the central inequality retains an explicit tail term for regeneration times.
sections.unique_caveat: One non-empirical term still depends on the tail behavior of regeneration times, and the framework requires regenerative structure.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper has a substantive bridge across probability, statistics, and machine learning: one concentration inequality supports generalization, oracle, minimax-deviation, and Gaussian-approximation claims.

sections.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
sections.abstract: For univariate Gaussian mixtures, the authors establish minimax squared-Hellinger rates for the unconstrained NPMLE under sub-Gaussian mixing and for a compactly constrained NPMLE under compactly supported mixing.
sections.claimed_result: With n i.i.d. observations, the unconstrained NPMLE attains squared-Hellinger rate log n/n for sub-Gaussian mixing; with compactly supported mixing, the interval-constrained NPMLE attains log n/(n log log n) (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Density estimation for univariate Gaussian mixtures from independent identically distributed samples; the two rates require, respectively, a sub-Gaussian true mixing measure or compact support and a matching compact constraint.
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantees are tied to the stated mixing-measure classes; they do not establish the same rates for unrestricted heavy-tailed mixing distributions.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper states matching minimax-optimal rates in two different mixing-measure regimes and derives a cross-application to Gaussian empirical Bayes, spanning statistics, information theory, and machine learning.

sections.title: On ABP Estimates for a Class of Fully Nonlinear Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations and Applications
sections.abstract: The authors extend an Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci estimate to fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and gradient dependence, then apply it to several nonlinear PDE classes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish a weighted ABP-type bound for classical subsolutions and viscosity subsolutions with locally Lipschitz gradients; it yields sup-norm estimates for the stated equation families (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and nonlinear gradient dependence; growth rates are general, but a smallness condition is imposed when the associated gradient weight is integrable.
sections.unique_caveat: The Hessian-quotient application requires an additional condition on the contact Hessian; the theorem is not a blanket estimate for all fully nonlinear elliptic equations.
sections.ranking_evidence: The result extends a foundational sup-norm estimate to a broader coefficient/gradient regime and lists applications to Monge--Ampère, Hessian, Hessian-quotient, and anisotropic mean-curvature-type equations.

sections.title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
sections.abstract: The author classifies real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds: none occur in dimensions 2 and 3, while in dimensions at least 4 the parallel distributions split globally as a product.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves nonexistence in dimensions 2 and 3 and a global product splitting of the two parallel distributions for every compact simply connected real-analytic example of dimension at least 4 (arXiv abstract).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact simply connected manifold equipped with a real-analytic conformal product structure, dimension n≥2.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is in the real-analytic, compact, simply connected setting; it does not classify smooth structures on non-simply-connected manifolds.
sections.ranking_evidence: It supplies an all-dimensions classification with a clear low-dimensional nonexistence/high-dimensional splitting dichotomy, complementing the selected rigidity paper in differential geometry.
